title: FDA approval of Enovid, the first contraceptive pill
summary: On 11 May 1960 the US Food and Drug Administration announced it had approved G.D. Searle's Enovid as an oral contraceptive, for no more than two years of use at a time. Margaret Sanger and Katharine McCormick backed the research by Gregory Pincus, Min-Chueh Chang and John Rock, some of it unethical by today's standards. Enovid gave women a new means of controlling pregnancy and led the way for later pills.

uncertainty.note: 11 May 1960 is the announcement date given by PBS; another source says summer 1960.

as_recorded.value: on May 11, 1960, the FDA officially announced its approval of the contraceptive pill
It was not until 1960 that the same drug was submitted to FDA for approval specifically as an oral contraceptive
In the summer of 1960, Enovid received approval from the Food and Drug Administration to be marketed as the first oral birth control pill

importance.justification: The first drug approved to prevent pregnancy, giving women a new means of family planning used worldwide.
